findings: plan_aggregate.cpp: the larger perfect-HA mode (up to 22 bits) has general guards. The estimated input must be at least slots/2. The thread-local tables plus the global table must fit in max_memory/8. It stays off when the user lowers perfect_ht_threshold below the default 12, and when the input contains a DELIM_SCAN. None of these conditions names a query, table or literal. They cover any dense integer-keyed GROUP BY, such as foreign-key aggregates over fact tables.

perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp: lazy slot initialization looks correct. AddChunk initializes a slot the first time it is set, CombineRange initializes a target slot before combining into it, and Scan and Destroy only visit slots that are set. Empty input and NULL groups (which have their own null slot) are handled.

Striped Combine: the stripes cover disjoint ranges of the data and group_is_set arrays, and each stripe has its own lock. Each thread uses only its own local table's allocator while combining. TakeAllocator is serialized under the global lock. I found no data race.

Parallel source: blocks of 64K slots are handed out through an atomic cursor. Each thread has its own scratch addresses and arena, and the group values are kept on the stack. SourceOrder was already NO_ORDER, and tables of 16 bits or fewer are still one block.

Minor, not blocking: in AddChunk, group_is_set[group] is set before InitializeStates runs, which only happens after the loop. If the out-of-range InternalException fires partway through a chunk (this needs incorrect statistics), slots earlier in that chunk are marked set but never initialized. Destroy would then call destroy on garbage states. Checking the range before marking slots, or initializing before the throw, would close this. It only happens on an internal-error path.
